title: arXiv AI notable papers — Tuesday, 10 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred, relevance-ranked selection, not a popularity ranking. Citation evidence for papers announced in this batch is limited.

sections.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
sections.abstract: WorkflowArena introduces 145 long-horizon tasks across eight professional domains to measure whether LLM agents can construct and adapt executable multi-agent workflows, with hidden verification of final deliverables.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose evaluating workflow orchestration as a distinct capability and report that, in a fixed-executor transfer experiment, workflows from one source model improve weaker executors.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report one evaluation per task without variance estimates; for some deliverables, LLM-judge agreement with human graders was not measured, and workflow transfer uses a subset with two source models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strongest outside-attention signal found in this set: AGI Hunt surfaces practitioner discussion, and arXivSignals separately indexes the paper; its 145-task, eight-domain benchmark also gives it unusually broad evaluation scope. These are secondary coverage signals, not readership or citation counts.

sections.title: AutoBuddy: Evaluating Proactive, Always-On Agents on Task Discovery and Execution in a Simulated Workplace
sections.abstract: AutoBuddy-Bench simulates a workplace to test whether agents can discover outstanding tasks in workspace records and then execute them, separating discovery from completion.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a temporal-graph workplace simulator and reference agent; their evaluation finds that task discovery and task execution behave as distinct capabilities, with stronger models often failing during business-system operations.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported results come from a generated simulated organization and 120 tasks; the paper's evidence does not establish transfer to live enterprise workspaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper spans two core AI categories and evaluates 17 backbones over 120 tasks, with separate discovery and execution measures; several secondary paper-indexing services surfaced it. The ranking reflects its direct fit to agent evaluation, not measured readership.

sections.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
sections.abstract: The authors formulate oversight as a game between an agent and a trajectory-monitoring monitor whose claims are checked by a verifier, and report tests on three agentic settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define a Subgame-Perfect Oversight Equilibrium, prove existence for finite games, and state that faithfulness follows with a perfect verifier—or with an imperfect verifier whose errors do not reverse monitor-action rankings.
sections.unique_caveat: The theoretical guarantee depends on verifier quality; empirically, the reported evaluations use Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B in three benchmark settings, not unrestricted deployments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Its formal equilibrium analysis is paired with empirical comparisons on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop, giving it evidence across theory and multiple test settings. Independent attention evidence was not established in the sources checked.

sections.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
sections.abstract: HiVe-Mem links retrieved episodes through textual and visual anchors and selects among multiple evidence forms per memory, reporting improved performance and about 90% lower token use than the most efficient competing multimodal baselines on three benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine graph-based expansion of semantically retrieved memories with a trainable, query-adaptive selector over summaries, captions, visual views, images, and interaction history.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports benchmark results but does not establish performance in deployed, open-ended long-term interactions; the 90% token reduction is relative to the competing baselines tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in three core AI categories, with evaluations across three multimodal-memory benchmarks and a concrete token-use comparison; multiple secondary discovery listings surfaced the paper. The reported gains are author results, not independent replications.

sections.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
sections.abstract: RoboScript rehearses a single demonstration in simulation and stores the resulting task knowledge in context rather than updating model weights; the authors report 83.4% mean success on 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and transfer to a physical dual-arm robot.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose World In-Context Learning, where simulator feedback is written into task memory for deployment without gradient updates, and report performance above the strongest trained action policy on their benchmark.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence centers on RoboTwin 2.0 and a physical dual-arm transfer demonstration; the abstract does not establish broad robustness across robot platforms or task families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The cross-list connects vision and robotics; the paper reports a 50-task benchmark, randomized settings, and a physical-robot transfer demonstration. Those provide a broad empirical case, though independent uptake was not confirmed.

sections.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
sections.abstract: Reframe trains visual agents to use tool-returned observations and repairs deficient tool actions during distillation; the authors report improvements over Mix-RL and vanilla multi-teacher on-policy distillation on 14 image and video benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Ground-Drop-GRPO and Observation-Gated-MOPD, aligning training with the observations available after tool use rather than only with output distributions.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence summarized in the abstract is benchmark-based; deployment beyond the tested image and video tasks is not established there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Fourteen image/video benchmarks and ablations on observation dependence give the paper substantial evaluation breadth; it is a core-corpus vision submission. No independent attention signal was verified.

sections.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
sections.abstract: In controlled transformer pretraining experiments, the authors find that NVFP4 models can need more exposures than BF16 models to match rare-fact recall even when validation losses are similar, and propose tracking rare-fact acquisition alongside loss.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report higher exposure requirements under NVFP4 across synthetic-biography and mixed-web-text settings, and suggest evaluating rare-fact acquisition in addition to validation loss.
sections.unique_caveat: The experiments use controlled synthetic biographies and mixtures with web text; they do not establish the same exposure cost for large-scale production pretraining.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The study supplies a controlled, quantifiable measurement linking precision format to rare-fact recall and a proposed diagnostic, making it a distinct and testable training result; it has no cross-list breadth or independent attention evidence in the sources checked.
